script: Am I the jerk for ruining my brothers girlfriends postpartum. I have one brother, 33 year old male. He never had a boyfriend until last year. He met his girlfriend, 32, and two months in she got pregnant. We were all like, "Oh my god, baby!" and the family was buzzing. She started talking a lot about cutting people out of her life if they didn't agree with her. So we, the whole crew, decided to keep it tight around her—no unsolicited advice, no questions about delivery, no visitors. I got a 9‑page document from her, a postpartum manifesto about how she wanted to listen to her body. I didn't question it. I've had five kids, so it felt normal, even if it was a lot. Fast forward to the birth. We were on a holiday, she sent us pictures. We were happy. When we got back, I pinged my brother and asked him to let us know when they wanted visitors. He said, "Come after work tomorrow." I told him I'd let him know if he changed his mind. The next day I showed up. He said we could come. We ate dinner, brought them some goodies, stayed for about 30 minutes, then left. All good. Six weeks later, my brother's girlfriend posted online: "A father doesn't love his kids if…." She listed reasons. I thought, "I agree, but it's a two‑sided street, right? Maybe she should switch the word 'father' to 'parent.'" I typed that. She had a full‑blown online tantrum, calling me disgusting for putting family business on social. I apologized via text, but she didn't take it. I called my brother, tried to explain, but he said he didn't get why she was mad. He asked if I could call her again. I did. I said, "If I had any more concerns, I'd talk to her personally, not online." I thought that was the end. Then, about seven weeks after the baby was born, she texted me: "You ruined my postpartum. You added stress." I apologized again, admitted I shouldn't have commented, but I still believe relationships are a two‑way street. I know I should have kept my wack ideas to myself and walked on eggshells, and I regret it. Still, I don't think one comment ruined her postpartum. I am the one who's upset that I am being called a jerk. We have a family gathering this weekend. I am dreading it but also looking forward to seeing my niece and brother. Am I the jerk for commenting on something she posted publicly and "ruining" her postpartum?
